verses.zh: 耶 穌 設 一 個 比 喻 ， 是 要 人 常 常 禱 告 ， 不 可 灰 心 。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] Jesus[NOTE:2] told them a parable to show them they should always[NOTE:3] pray and not lose heart.[NOTE:4]
notes: Here δὲ (de) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.
Grk “he”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Or “should pray at all times” (L&N 67.88).
This is one of the few parables that comes with an explanation at the start:…they should always pray and not lose heart. It is part of Luke’s goal in encouraging Theophilus (1:4).

verses.zh: 說 ： 某 城 裡 有 一 個 官 ， 不 懼 怕 神 ， 也 不 尊 重 世 人 。
verses.en: He said,[NOTE:1] “In a certain city[NOTE:2] there was a judge[NOTE:3] who neither feared God nor respected people.[NOTE:4]
notes: Grk “lose heart, saying.” This is a continuation of the previous sentence in the Greek text, but a new sentence was started here in the translation by supplying the pronominal subject “He.”
Or “town.”
The judge here is apparently portrayed as a civil judge who often handled financial cases.
Grk “man,” but the singular ἄνθρωπος (anthrōpos) is used as a generic in comparison to God.

verses.zh: 那 城 裡 有 個 寡 婦 ， 常 到 他 那 裡 ， 說 ： 我 有 一 個 對 頭 ， 求 你 給 我 伸 冤 。
verses.en: There was also a widow[NOTE:1] in that city[NOTE:2] who kept coming[NOTE:3] to him and saying, ‘Give me justice against my adversary.’
notes: This widow was not necessarily old, since many people lived only into their thirties in the 1st century.
Or “town.”
This is an iterative imperfect; the widow did this on numerous occasions.

verses.zh: 他 多 日 不 准 。 後 來 心 裡 說 ： 我 雖 不 懼 怕 神 ， 也 不 尊 重 世 人 ，
verses.en: For[NOTE:1] a while he refused, but later on[NOTE:2] he said to himself, ‘Though I neither fear God nor have regard for people,[NOTE:3]
notes: Grk “And for.” Here καί (kai) has not been translated because of differences between Greek and English style.
Grk “after these things.”
Grk “man,” but the singular ἄνθρωπος (anthrōpos) is used as a generic in comparison to God.

verses.zh: 只 因 這 寡 婦 煩 擾 我 ， 我 就 給 他 伸 冤 罷 ， 免 得 他 常 來 纏 磨 我 ！
verses.en: yet because this widow keeps on bothering me, I will give her justice, or in the end she will wear me out[NOTE:1] by her unending pleas.’”[NOTE:2]
notes: The term ὑπωπιάζω (hupōpiazō) in this context means “to wear someone out by continual annoying” (L&N 25.245).
Grk “by her continual coming,” but the point of annoyance to the judge is her constant pleas for justice (v. 3).

verses.zh: 主 說 ： 你 們 聽 這 不 義 之 官 所 說 的 話 。
verses.en: And the Lord said, “Listen to what the unrighteous judge says![NOTE:1]
notes: Listen to what the unrighteous judge says! The point of the parable is that the judge’s lack of compassion was overcome by the widow’s persistence.

verses.zh: 神 的 選 民 晝 夜 呼 籲 他 ， 他 縱 然 為 他 們 忍 了 多 時 ， 豈 不 終 久 給 他 們 伸 冤 麼 ？
verses.en: Won’t[NOTE:1] God give justice to his chosen ones, who cry out[NOTE:2] to him day and night?[NOTE:3] Will he delay[NOTE:4] long to help them?
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated.
The prayers have to do with the righteous who cry out to him to receive justice. The context assumes the righteous are persecuted.
The emphatic particles in this sentence indicate that God will indeed give justice to the righteous.

The issue of delay has produced a whole host of views for this verse. (1) Does this assume provision to endure in the meantime? Or (2) does it mean God restricts the level of persecution until he comes? Either view is possible.

verses.zh: 我 告 訴 你 們 ， 要 快 快 的 給 他 們 伸 冤 了 。 然 而 ， 人 子 來 的 時 候 ， 遇 得 見 世 上 有 信 德 麼 ？
verses.en: I tell you, he will give them justice speedily.[NOTE:1] Nevertheless, when the Son of Man comes, will he find faith[NOTE:2] on earth?”
notes: Some argue this should be translated “suddenly.” When vindication comes it will be quick. But the more natural meaning is “soon.” God will not forget his elect and will respond to them. It may be that this verse has a prophetic perspective. In light of the eternity that comes, vindication is soon.
Will he find faith on earth? The Son of Man is looking for those who continue to believe in him, despite the wait.

verses.zh: 耶 穌 向 那 些 仗 著 自 己 是 義 人 ， 藐 視 別 人 的 ， 設 一 個 比 喻 ，
verses.en: Jesus[NOTE:1] also told this parable to some who were confident that they were righteous and looked down[NOTE:2] on everyone else.
notes: Grk “He”; the referent has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Grk “and despised.” This is a second parable with an explanatory introduction.

verses.zh: 說 ： 有 兩 個 人 上 殿 裡 去 禱 告 ： 一 個 是 法 利 賽 人 ， 一 個 是 稅 吏 。
verses.en: “Two men went up[NOTE:1] to the temple to pray, one a Pharisee[NOTE:2] and the other a tax collector.[NOTE:3]
notes: The temple is on a hill in Jerusalem, so one would go up to enter its precincts.
See the note on Pharisees in 5:17.
See the note on tax collectors in 3:12.

verses.zh: 法 利 賽 人 站 著 ， 自 言 自 語 的 禱 告 說 ： 神 阿 ， 我 感 謝 你 ， 我 不 像 別 人 勒 索 、 不 義 、 姦 淫 ， 也 不 像 這 個 稅 吏 。
verses.en: The Pharisee stood and prayed about himself like this:[NOTE:1] ‘God, I thank[NOTE:2] you that I am not like other people:[NOTE:3] extortionists,[NOTE:4] unrighteous people,[NOTE:5] adulterers—or even like this tax collector.[NOTE:6]
notes: Or “stood by himself and prayed like this.” The prepositional phrase πρὸς ἑαυτόν (pros eauton, “to/about himself”) could go with either the aorist participle σταθείς (statheis, “stood”) or with the imperfect verb προσηύχετο (prosēucheto, “he prayed”). If taken with the participle, then the meaning would seem at first glance to be: “stood ‘by himself’,” or “stood ‘alone’.” Now it is true that πρός can mean “by” or “with” when used with intransitive verbs such as ἵστημι (histēmi, “I stand”; cf. BDAG 874 s.v. πρός 2.a), but πρὸς ἑαυτόν together never means “by himself” or “alone” in biblical Greek. On the other hand, if πρὸς ἑαυτόν is taken with the verb, then two different nuances emerge, both of which highlight in different ways the principal point Jesus seems to be making about the arrogance of this religious leader: (1) “prayed to himself,” but not necessarily silently, or (2) “prayed about himself,” with the connotation that he prayed out loud, for all to hear. Since his prayer is really a review of his moral résumé, directed both at advertising his own righteousness and exposing the perversion of the tax collector, whom he actually mentions in his prayer, the latter option seems preferable. If this is the case, then the Pharisee’s mention of God is really nothing more than a formality.
The Pharisee’s prayer started out as a thanksgiving psalm to God, but the praise ended up not being about God.
Here the plural Greek term ἀνθρώπων (anthrōpōn) is used as a generic and can refer to both men and women (NASB, NRSV, “people”; NLT, “everyone else”; NAB, “the rest of humanity”).
Or “swindlers” (BDAG 134 s.v. ἅρπαξ 2); see also Isa 10:2; Josephus, J. W. 6.3.4 [6.203].
A general category for “sinners” (1 Cor 6:9; Lev 19:3).
Note what the Pharisee assumes about the righteousness of this tax collector by grouping him with extortionists, unrighteous people, and adulterers.

verses.zh: 我 一 個 禮 拜 禁 食 兩 次 ， 凡 我 所 得 的 都 捐 上 十 分 之 一 。
verses.en: I fast twice[NOTE:1] a week; I give a tenth[NOTE:2] of everything I get.’
notes: The law only required fasting on the Day of Atonement. Such voluntary fasting as this practiced twice a week by the Pharisee normally took place on Monday and Thursday.
Or “I tithe.”

verses.zh: 那 稅 吏 遠 遠 的 站 著 ， 連 舉 目 望 天 也 不 敢 ， 只 捶 著 胸 說 ： 神 阿 ， 開 恩 可 憐 我 這 個 罪 人 ！
verses.en: The tax collector, however, stood[NOTE:1] far off and would not even look up[NOTE:2] to heaven, but beat his breast and said, ‘God, be merciful[NOTE:3] to me, sinner that I am!’[NOTE:4]
notes: Grk “standing”; the Greek participle has been translated as a finite verb.
Grk “even lift up his eyes” (an idiom).
The prayer is a humble call for forgiveness. The term for mercy (ἱλάσκομαι, hilaskomai) is associated with the concept of a request for atonement (BDAG 473-74 s.v. 1; Pss 51:1, 3; 25:11; 34:6, 18).
Grk “the sinner.” The tax collector views himself not just as any sinner but as the worst of all sinners. See ExSyn 222-23.

verses.zh: 我 告 訴 你 們 ， 這 人 回 家 去 比 那 人 倒 算 為 義 了 ； 因 為 ， 凡 自 高 的 ， 必 降 為 卑 ； 自 卑 的 ， 必 升 為 高 。
verses.en: I tell you that this man went down to his home justified[NOTE:1] rather than the Pharisee.[NOTE:2] For everyone who exalts[NOTE:3] himself will be humbled, but he who humbles himself will be exalted.”
notes: The prayer that was heard and honored was the one given with humility; in a surprising reversal it was the tax collector who went down to his home justified.
Grk “the other”; the referent (the Pharisee, v. 10) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Everyone who exalts himself. See Luke 14:11. Jesus often called for humility and condemned those who sought honor.

verses.zh: 有 人 抱 著 自 己 的 嬰 孩 來 見 耶 穌 ， 要 他 摸 他 們 ； 門 徒 看 見 就 責 備 那 些 人 。
verses.en: Now people[NOTE:1] were even bringing their babies[NOTE:2] to him for him to touch.[NOTE:3] But when the disciples saw it, they began to scold those who brought them.[NOTE:4]
notes: Grk “they.”
The term βρέφος (brephos) here can refer to babies or to toddlers (2:12, 16; Acts 7:19; 2 Tim 3:15; 1 Pet 2:2).
Grk “so that he would touch them.” Here the touch is connected with (or conveys) a blessing (cf. Mark 10:16; also BDAG 126 s.v. ἅπτω 2.c).

Grk “the disciples began to scold them.” In the translation the referent has been specified as “those who brought them,” since otherwise the statement could be understood to mean that the disciples began scolding the children rather than their parents who brought them.

verses.zh: 耶 穌 卻 叫 他 們 來 ， 說 ： 讓 小 孩 子 到 我 這 裡 來 ， 不 要 禁 止 他 們 ； 因 為 在 神 國 的 正 是 這 樣 的 人 。
verses.en: But Jesus called for the children,[NOTE:1] saying, “Let the little children come to me and do not try to stop them, for the kingdom of God[NOTE:2] belongs to such as these.[NOTE:3]
notes: Grk “summoned them”; the referent (the children) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

The kingdom of God is a major theme of Jesus’ teaching. The nature of the kingdom of God in the NT and in Jesus’ teaching has long been debated by interpreters and scholars, with discussion primarily centering around the nature of the kingdom (earthly, heavenly, or both) and the kingdom’s arrival (present, future, or both). An additional major issue concerns the relationship between the kingdom of God and the person and work of Jesus himself. See Luke 6:20; 11:20; 17:20-21.

The kingdom of God belongs to such as these. Children are a picture of those whose simple trust illustrates what faith is all about. The remark illustrates how everyone is important to God, even those whom others regard as insignificant.

verses.zh: 我 實 在 告 訴 你 們 ， 凡 要 承 受 神 國 的 ， 若 不 像 小 孩 子 ， 斷 不 能 進 去 。
verses.en: I tell you the truth,[NOTE:1] whoever does not receive[NOTE:2] the kingdom of God like a child[NOTE:3] will never[NOTE:4] enter it.”
notes: Grk “Truly (ἀμήν, amēn), I say to you.”
On receive see John 1:12.

The point of the comparison receive the kingdom of God like a child has more to do with a child’s trusting spirit and willingness to be dependent and receive from others than any inherent humility the child might possess.
The negation in Greek used here (οὐ μή, ou mē) is very strong.

verses.zh: 有 一 個 官 問 耶 穌 說 ： 良 善 的 夫 子 ， 我 該 做 甚 麼 事 才 可 以 承 受 永 生 ？
verses.en: Now[NOTE:1] a certain leader[NOTE:2] asked him, “Good teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?”[NOTE:3]
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “now” to indicate the transition to a new topic.

Only Luke states this man is a leader (cf. the parallels in Matt 19:16-22 and Mark 10:17-22, where the questioner is described only as “someone”). He is probably a civic leader of some kind, a leader in the society.tn Grk “a certain ruler.” BDAG 140 s.v. ἄρχων 2.a takes this to be a member of the Sanhedrin, but Bock understands this to be “an influential wealthy man or civic leader who may have been known for his piety” (D. L. Bock, Luke [BECNT] 2:1476).

The rich man wanted to know what he must do to inherit eternal life, but Jesus had just finished teaching that eternal life was not earned but simply received (18:17). See the similar question about inheriting eternal life in Luke 10:25.

verses.zh: 耶 穌 對 他 說 ： 你 為 甚 麼 稱 我 是 良 善 的 ？ 除 了 神 一 位 之 外 ， 再 沒 有 良 善 的 。
verses.en: Jesus[NOTE:1] said to him, “Why do you call me good?[NOTE:2] No one is good except God alone.
notes: Grk “And Jesus.” Here καί (kai) has not been translated because of differences between Greek and English style.

Jesus’ response, Why do you call me good?, was designed to cause the ruler to stop and think for a moment about who Jesus really was. The following statement No one is good except God alone seems to point the man in the direction of Jesus’ essential nature and the demands which logically follow on the man for having said it.

verses.zh: 誡 命 你 是 曉 得 的 ： 不 可 姦 淫 ； 不 可 殺 人 ； 不 可 偷 盜 ； 不 可 作 假 見 證 ； 當 孝 敬 父 母 。
verses.en: You know the commandments: ‘Do not commit adultery, do not murder, do not steal, do not give false testimony, honor your father and mother.’”[NOTE:1]
notes: A quotation from Exod 20:12-16 and Deut 5:16-20. Jesus cited the parts of the ten commandments that relate to how others should be treated.

verses.zh: 那 人 說 ： 這 一 切 我 從 小 都 遵 守 了 。
verses.en: The man[NOTE:1] replied, “I have wholeheartedly obeyed[NOTE:2] all these laws[NOTE:3] since my youth.”[NOTE:4]
notes: Grk “And he”; the referent (the ruler mentioned in v. 18) has been specified in the translation for clarity. Here καί (kai) has not been translated because of differences between Greek and English style.

Grk “kept.” The implication of this verb is that the man has obeyed the commandments without fail throughout his life, so the adverb “wholeheartedly” has been added to the translation to bring out this nuance.

While the rich man was probably being sincere when he insisted I have wholeheartedly obeyed all these laws, he had confined his righteousness to external obedience. The rich man’s response to Jesus’ command to give away all he had revealed that internally he loved money more than God.tn Grk “these things.” The referent of the pronoun (the laws mentioned by Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Since my youth. Judaism regarded the age of thirteen as the age when a man would have become responsible to live by God’s commands.

verses.zh: 耶 穌 聽 見 了 ， 就 說 ： 你 還 缺 少 一 件 ： 要 變 賣 你 一 切 所 有 的 ， 分 給 窮 人 ， 就 必 有 財 寶 在 天 上 ； 你 還 要 來 跟 從 我 。
verses.en: When Jesus heard this, he said to him, “One thing you still lack. Sell all that you have[NOTE:1] and give the money[NOTE:2] to the poor,[NOTE:3] and you will have treasure[NOTE:4] in heaven. Then[NOTE:5] come, follow me.”
notes: See Luke 14:33.
The words “the money” are not in the Greek text, but are implied. Direct objects were frequently omitted in Greek when clear from the context.

The call for sacrifice comes with a promise of eternal reward:…you will have treasure in heaven. Jesus’ call is a test to see how responsive the man is to God’s direction through him. Will he walk the path God’s agent calls him to walk? For a rich person who got it right, see Zacchaeus in Luke 19:1-10.
Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the conversation.

verses.zh: 他 聽 見 這 話 ， 就 甚 憂 愁 ， 因 為 他 很 富 足 。
verses.en: But when the man[NOTE:1] heard this, he became very sad,[NOTE:2] for he was extremely wealthy.
notes: Grk “he”; the referent (the man) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Or “very distressed” (L&N 25.277).

verses.zh: 耶 穌 看 見 他 ， 就 說 ： 有 錢 財 的 人 進 神 的 國 是 何 等 的 難 哪 ！
verses.en: When Jesus noticed this,[NOTE:1] he said, “How hard[NOTE:2] it is for the rich to enter the kingdom of God![NOTE:3]
notes: Grk “him.”tc ‡ The phrase περίλυπον γενόμενον (perilupon genomenon, “[When Jesus saw him] becoming sad”) is found in the majority of mss (A [D] W Θ Ψ 078 ƒ13 33vid M latt sy), and it is not unknown in Lukan style to repeat a word or phrase in adjacent passages (TCGNT 143). However, the phrase is lacking in some significant mss (א B L ƒ1 579 1241 2542 co). The shorter reading is nevertheless difficult to explain if it is not autographic: It is possible that these witnesses omitted this phrase out of perceived redundancy from the preceding verse, although intentional omissions, especially by several and varied witnesses, are generally unlikely. NA28 places the words in brackets, indicating doubts as to their authenticity.

For the rich it is hard for wealth not to be the point of focus, as the contrast in vv. 28-30 will show, and for rich people to trust God. Wealth was not an automatic sign of blessing as far as Jesus was concerned.
The kingdom of God is a major theme of Jesus’ teaching. See the note on this phrase in v. 16.

verses.zh: 駱 駝 穿 過 針 的 眼 比 財 主 進 神 的 國 還 容 易 呢 ！
verses.en: In fact, it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle[NOTE:1] than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God.”
notes: The eye of a needle refers to a sewing needle, one of the smallest items one might deal with on a regular basis, in contrast to the biggest animal of the region. (Although the story of a small gate in Jerusalem known as “The Needle’s Eye” has been widely circulated and may go back as far as the middle ages, there is no evidence that such a gate ever existed.) Jesus is saying rhetorically that this is impossible, unless God (v. 27) intervenes.

verses.zh: 聽 見 的 人 說 ： 這 樣 ， 誰 能 得 救 呢 ？
verses.en: Those who heard this said, “Then[NOTE:1] who can be saved?”[NOTE:2]
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of thought.
The assumption is that the rich are blessed, so if they risk exclusion, who is left to be saved?

verses.zh: 耶 穌 說 ： 在 人 所 不 能 的 事 ， 在 神 卻 能 。
verses.en: He replied, “What is impossible[NOTE:1] for mere humans[NOTE:2] is possible for God.”
notes: The term impossible is in the emphatic position in the Greek text. God makes the impossible possible.

The plural Greek term ἄνθρωποις (anthrōpois) is used here in a generic sense, referring to both men and women (cf. NASB 1995 update, “people”). Because of the contrast here between mere mortals and God (“impossible for men…possible for God”) the phrase “mere humans” has been used in the translation.

verses.zh: 彼 得 說 ： 看 哪 ， 我 們 已 經 撇 下 自 己 所 有 的 跟 從 你 了 。
verses.en: And Peter said, “Look, we have left everything we own[NOTE:1] to follow you!
notes: Or “left our homes,” “left our possessions”; Grk “left our own things.” The word ἴδιος (idios) can refer to one’s home (including the people and possessions in it) or to one’s property or possessions. Both options are mentioned in BDAG 467 s.v. 4.b. See also I. H. Marshall, Luke (NIGTC), 688; D. L. Bock, Luke (BECNT), 2:1488.

verses.zh: 耶 穌 說 ： 我 實 在 告 訴 你 們 ， 人 為 神 的 國 撇 下 房 屋 ， 或 是 妻 子 、 弟 兄 、 父 母 、 兒 女 ，
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] Jesus[NOTE:2] said to them, “I tell you the truth,[NOTE:3] there is no one who has left home or wife or brothers[NOTE:4] or parents or children for the sake of God’s kingdom
notes: Here δέ (de) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.
Grk “he”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Grk “Truly (ἀμήν, amēn), I say to you.”

The term “brothers” could be understood as generic here, referring to either male or female siblings. However, it is noteworthy that in the parallel passages in both Matt 19:29 and Mark 10:29, “sisters” are explicitly mentioned in the Greek text.

verses.zh: 沒 有 在 今 世 不 得 百 倍 ， 在 來 世 不 得 永 生 的 。
verses.en: who will not receive many times more[NOTE:1] in this age[NOTE:2]—and in the age to come, eternal life.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Jesus reassures his disciples with a promise that (1) much benefit in this life (many times more) and (2) eternal life in the age to come will be given.
Grk “this time” (καιρός, kairos), but for stylistic reasons this has been translated “this age” here.

Note that Luke (see also Matt 19:29; Mark 10:30; Luke 10:25) portrays eternal life as something one receives in the age to come, unlike John, who emphasizes the possibility of receiving eternal life in the present (John 5:24).

verses.zh: 耶 穌 帶 著 十 二 個 門 徒 ， 對 他 們 說 ： 看 哪 ， 我 們 上 耶 路 撒 冷 去 ， 先 知 所 寫 的 一 切 事 都 要 成 就 在 人 子 身 上 。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] Jesus[NOTE:2] took the twelve aside and said to them, “Look, we are going up to Jerusalem,[NOTE:3] and everything that is written about the Son of Man by the prophets will be accomplished.[NOTE:4]
notes: Here δέ (de) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.
Grk “he”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
Or “fulfilled.” Jesus goes to Jerusalem by divine plan as the scripture records (Luke 2:39; 12:50; 22:37; Acts 13:29). See Luke 9:22, 44.

verses.zh: 他 將 要 被 交 給 外 邦 人 ， 他 們 要 戲 弄 他 ， 凌 辱 他 ， 吐 唾 沫 在 他 臉 上 ，
verses.en: For he will be handed over[NOTE:1] to the Gentiles; he will be mocked,[NOTE:2] mistreated,[NOTE:3] and spat on.[NOTE:4]
notes: The passive voice verb be handed over does not indicate by whom, but other passages note the Jewish leadership and betrayal (9:22, 44).
Or “and insulted.” L&N 33.390 and 88.130 note ὑβρίζω (hubrizō) can mean either “insult” or “mistreat with insolence.”
And spat on. Later Luke does not note this detail in the passion narrative in chaps. 22-23, but see Mark 14:65; 15:19; Matt 26:67; 27:30 where Jesus’ prediction is fulfilled.

verses.zh: 並 要 鞭 打 他 ， 殺 害 他 ； 第 三 日 他 要 復 活 。
verses.en: They will flog him severely[NOTE:1] and kill him. Yet[NOTE:2] on the third day he will rise again.”
notes: Traditionally, “scourge” (the term means to beat severely with a whip, L&N 19.9). BDAG 620 s.v. μαστιγόω 1. states, “Of the beating (Lat. verberatio) given those condemned to death…J 19:1; cf. Mt 20:19; Mk 10:34; Lk 18:33.” Here the term has been translated “flog…severely” to distinguish it from the term φραγελλόω (phragelloō) used in Matt 27:26; Mark 15:15.
Here καί (kai) has been translated as “yet” to indicate the contrast present in this context.

verses.zh: 這 些 事 門 徒 一 樣 也 不 懂 得 ， 意 思 乃 是 隱 藏 的 ； 他 們 不 曉 得 所 說 的 是 甚 麼 。
verses.en: But[NOTE:1] the twelve[NOTE:2] understood none of these things. This[NOTE:3] saying was hidden from them, and they did not grasp[NOTE:4] what Jesus meant.[NOTE:5]
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “but” to indicate the contrast.
Grk “they”; the referent (the twelve, v. 31) has been specified in the context for clarity.
Grk “And this.” Here καί (kai) has not been translated.

This failure of the Twelve to grasp what Jesus meant probably does not mean that they did not understand linguistically what Jesus said, but that they could not comprehend how this could happen to him, if he was really God’s agent. The saying being hidden probably refers to God’s sovereign timing.

Grk “the things having been said.” The active agent, Jesus, has been specified for clarity, and “said” has been translated as “meant” to indicate that comprehension of the significance is really in view here.

verses.zh: 耶 穌 將 近 耶 利 哥 的 時 候 ， 有 一 個 瞎 子 坐 在 路 旁 討 飯 。
verses.en: As[NOTE:1] Jesus[NOTE:2] approached[NOTE:3] Jericho,[NOTE:4] a blind man was sitting by the road begging.
notes: Grk “Now it happened that as.” The introductory phrase ἐγένετο (egeneto, “it happened that”), common in Luke (69 times) and Acts (54 times), is redundant in contemporary English and has not been translated.
Grk “he”; the referent (Jesus) has been supplied in the translation for clarity.

The phrase is “he drew near to” (19:29; 24:28). It is also possible the term merely means “is in the vicinity of.” Also possible is a reversal in the timing of the healing and Zacchaeus events for literary reasons as the blind man “sees” where the rich man with everything did not.
For location see Map5-B2; Map6-E1; Map7-E1; Map8-E3; Map10-A2; Map11-A1.

verses.zh: 聽 見 許 多 人 經 過 ， 就 問 是 甚 麼 事 。
verses.en: When he heard a crowd going by, he asked what was going on.

verses.zh: 他 們 告 訴 他 ， 是 拿 撒 勒 人 耶 穌 經 過 。
verses.en: They[NOTE:1] told him, “Jesus the Nazarene is passing by.”
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated. “They” could refer to bystanders or people in the crowd.

verses.zh: 他 就 呼 叫 說 ： 大 衛 的 子 孫 耶 穌 阿 ， 可 憐 我 罷 ！
verses.en: So[NOTE:1] he called out,[NOTE:2] “Jesus, Son of David,[NOTE:3] have mercy[NOTE:4] on me!”
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “so” to indicate the implied result of the blind man learning that Jesus was nearby.
Grk “called out, saying.” The participle λέγων (legōn) is redundant in contemporary English and has not been translated.

Jesus was more than a Nazarene to this blind person, who saw quite well that Jesus was Son of David. He understood what Luke 7:22-23 affirms. There was a tradition in Judaism that the Son of David (Solomon) had great powers of healing (Josephus, Ant. 8.2.5 [8.42-49]).
Have mercy on me is a request for healing (cf. 17:13). It is not owed the man. He simply asks for God’s kind grace.

verses.zh: 在 前 頭 走 的 人 就 責 備 他 ， 不 許 他 作 聲 ； 他 卻 越 發 喊 叫 說 ： 大 衛 的 子 孫 ， 可 憐 我 罷 ！
verses.en: And those who were in front[NOTE:1] scolded[NOTE:2] him to get him to be quiet, but he shouted[NOTE:3] even more, “Son of David, have mercy on me!”
notes: That is, those who were at the front of the procession.
Or “rebuked.” The crowd’s view was that surely Jesus would not be bothered with someone as unimportant as a blind beggar.
Public opinion would not sway the blind man from getting Jesus’ attention. The term shouted is strong as it can be used of animal cries.

verses.zh: 耶 穌 站 住 ， 吩 咐 把 他 領 過 來 ， 到 了 跟 前 ， 就 問 他 說 ：
verses.en: So[NOTE:1] Jesus stopped and ordered the beggar[NOTE:2] to be brought to him. When the man[NOTE:3] came near, Jesus[NOTE:4] asked him,
notes: Here δέ (de) has been translated as “so” to indicate the implied result of the beggar’s cries.
Grk “ordered him”; the referent (the blind beggar, v. 35) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Grk “he”; the referent (the beggar) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Grk “he”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 你 要 我 為 你 做 甚 麼 ？ 他 說 ： 主 阿 ， 我 要 能 看 見 。
verses.en: “What do you want me to do for you?” He replied,[NOTE:1] “Lord, let me see again.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “said.”

Grk “Lord, that I may see [again].” The phrase can be rendered as an imperative of request, “Please, give me sight.” Since the man is not noted as having been blind from birth (as the man in John 9 was) it is likely the request is to receive back the sight he once had.

verses.zh: 耶 穌 說 ： 你 可 以 看 見 ！ 你 的 信 救 了 你 了 。
verses.en: Jesus[NOTE:1] said to him, “Receive[NOTE:2] your sight; your faith has healed you.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated because of differences between Greek and English style.
Or “Regain” (see the note on the phrase “let me see again” in the previous verse).
Grk “has saved you,” but in a nonsoteriological sense; the man has been delivered from his disability.

verses.zh: 瞎 子 立 刻 看 見 了 ， 就 跟 隨 耶 穌 ， 一 路 歸 榮 耀 與 神 。 眾 人 看 見 這 事 ， 也 讚 美 神 。
verses.en: And immediately he regained[NOTE:1] his sight and followed Jesus,[NOTE:2] praising[NOTE:3] God. When[NOTE:4] all the people saw it, they too[NOTE:5] gave praise to God.
notes: Or “received” (see the note on the phrase “let me see again” in v. 41).
Grk “him”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
The presence of God’s work leads again to joy, with both the beggar and the people praising God (1:64; 2:20; 5:25-26; 7:16; 13:13; 17:15; 19:37).
Here καί (kai) has not been translated because of differences between Greek and English style.
The word “too” has been supplied for stylistic reasons.
